findings.category: continuity — residual of the F-01 repair
findings.gate: Craft Core — Reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); r1 F-01 repair_target (which named line 11)

draft_evidence.quote: The lamp went on into the middle gallery, and there was a second light at the end of it that had not come with them.

comparison_evidence.quote: and Cleon, behind him, pulled the iron to, and the tiers closed, and the dark opened.

findings.consequence: Under the r1 staging Cleon had been below for an hour, so his lamp genuinely had not come with them and line 11 was clean. The repair correctly moved him into the party at the door — Ch9 has him enter last and shut the iron behind Cael — and then sends him ahead with his own lamp (l.19). His lamp therefore did come with them, and the only light at the gallery's end that did not is the always-lit table lamp introduced eight lines later (l.17). A reader arriving at l.11 has no way to know that yet and will most naturally read the second light as Cleon's, which l.19 then contradicts. The line 11 clause named in the r1 repair_target was left unedited.
findings.repair_target: ch10.md line 11 — make the light the one that was already burning rather than one that did not travel ('a second light at the end of it that had been burning before they came', or 'a light at the end of it that nobody had carried down'). Do not restore the hour.

draft_evidence.quote: "I know that hand." He did not say from where. "You've brought it in off the ground. Three floors of it. Do you know what that is, to a man who's been sitting in a hole for thirty years being tolerated?"

comparison_evidence.quote: "In thirty years I never had the stone to match the text. You walked in with three floors." A beat. "I don't think you're going to like what you've found, Karis. I've had a piece of it for a decade and I've never once slept well since."

findings.consequence: Three of F-03's four pre-paid clauses are cleanly gone and the fourth (the sleeplessness) has been converted into a plant — 'you'll not sleep either' at l.45 — which Ch11 then explains. What survives is the fourth clause of the Ch11 closer's structure: Cleon crediting Karis with having brought him three floors, in the same speaker's voice, one chapter early and with the same shape. Ch11's 'You walked in with three floors' is fixed card text and cannot be moved, so on the page it will read as the same man making the same remark twice inside four days, which blunts the closer the card exists to protect. This is the smaller half of a HIGH finding, not a new defect, and it is the last piece of Ch11 still sitting in Ch10.
findings.repair_target: ch10.md line 41 — keep 'I know that hand.' and the withholding, and let Cleon name what is in front of him without crediting the delivery ('You've brought it in off the ground' → 'It's off the ground' / 'This came off a floor'), leaving 'You walked in with three floors' to Ch11. The word 'three floors' itself is Karis's at l.31–33 and can stay there.
